symbol.pick: What is the standard symbol for the {label}?
symbol.match: Match each unit to its symbol.

rows.label: parsec
rows.description: unit of length used in astronomy
rows.hook: measures the vast gaps between stars, equal to about 3.26 light-years

rows.label: joule
rows.description: SI unit of energy, work and amount of heat
rows.hook: measures energy and is named after an English brewer-turned-physicist

rows.label: degree Fahrenheit
rows.hook: measures temperature on the scale where water freezes at 32 and boils at 212

rows.label: degree Celsius
rows.hook: measures temperature on the scale where water freezes at zero and boils at 100

rows.label: kelvin
rows.hook: measures temperature on a scale that starts at absolute zero

rows.label: decibel
rows.description: logarithmic unit expressing the ratio of a physical quantity
rows.hook: measures how loud a sound is, on a logarithmic scale

rows.label: metre
rows.hook: is the base unit of length in the metric system, a little longer than a yard

rows.label: pascal
rows.description: SI unit of pressure and stress
rows.hook: measures pressure and is named after a French mathematician and philosopher

rows.label: hertz
rows.hook: counts cycles per second, used for radio stations and sound pitch

rows.label: watt
rows.hook: measures electrical power and is named after the Scottish inventor who improved the steam engine

rows.label: newton
rows.hook: measures force and is named after the scientist said to have been inspired by a falling apple

rows.label: astronomical unit
rows.description: mean distance between Earth and the Sun, common length reference in astronomy
rows.hook: is roughly the distance from our planet to its star, about 150 million kilometres

rows.label: byte
rows.description: unit of digital information equal to 8 bits
rows.hook: is the amount of computer storage needed to hold a single character, made of eight bits

rows.label: knot
rows.hook: measures how fast ships and aircraft travel, one nautical mile per hour

rows.label: ampere
rows.hook: measures the flow of electric current and is named after a French physicist

rows.label: hectare
rows.hook: measures land area, equal to a 100-metre by 100-metre square

rows.label: kilogram
rows.hook: is the base unit of weight in the metric system, defined for years by a platinum cylinder kept in France

rows.label: mile
rows.hook: is the imperial distance a runner covers in a four-lap race on a standard track

rows.label: coulomb
rows.hook: measures electric charge and is named after a French physicist who studied static attraction

rows.label: kilometre
rows.description: SI unit of length equal to one thousand metres
rows.hook: is a thousand of the base metric length, the way road distances are given in most countries

rows.label: electronvolt
rows.hook: measures the tiny energy an electron gains crossing one volt, used in particle physics

rows.label: gigabyte
rows.description: unit of digital information equal to one billion bytes or 1,000 megabytes
rows.hook: is how phone and computer storage is commonly sold, a thousand million of the basic data unit

rows.label: volt
rows.description: SI unit of electric potential, of electric potential difference (voltage), and of electromotive force
rows.hook: measures electrical pressure and is named after an Italian who invented the battery

rows.label: radian
rows.hook: measures angles using the radius of a circle, with pi times two around a full turn

rows.label: foot
rows.hook: is the imperial length famously twelve inches long, and how airplane altitude is reported

rows.label: lumen
rows.hook: measures how bright a light bulb is, the total visible light it puts out

rows.label: litre
rows.description: unit of volume accepted for use with the SI
rows.hook: is the metric measure for soft drink bottles and milk, about a quart
